title: Old and odd elements: font, marquee, xmp, blink, a foreign iframe and a footer
blurb: A 1990s page of <center>, <font> and <marquee> on the tube of a drawn monitor, an <xmp> whose tags the canvas colours, an audit that outlines unknown elements, a warning over frames the canvas can't draw, and a footer that lies on the ground with links that still work.
question: What does a canvas get from elements at the edges of HTML (font and marquee, xmp, names the parser doesn't know, a frame from another origin, a footer used as a floor), and what does it have to find out another way?
result: In Chromium 157 old and unknown elements are all in the picture, and a marquee inside a drawable block raised 60 paint events a second. A frame from another origin is left out (alpha 0) and still takes taps; a null contentDocument finds it. An xmp has no child elements, so its tags are coloured from Range rectangles. updateElementGeometry() takes a perspective matrix on a 2D canvas, so links on a slanted footer are hit-tested by the browser.
